name: Orbit AI - CRM Architecture - Contract Amendment Flow (05 Section 7/13, new - not brief-W-numbered)

nodes.name: Contract amendment webhook
nodes.notes: 05 Section 7/13: 'any material change to an existing Contract (Location added/removed, service tier changed) triggers versioning + an Accounting Audit Event, NOT an edit in place' - specifically for a change originating from the SAME Company already holding the Contract (an unrelated Company hitting an active Location is location-contract-lock-check.workflow.json's job instead, not this one). Input contract: {companyId, oldContractId, opportunityId (the expansion deal driving this - required, since 'Deal stage on the affected record moves to Expansion' needs a record), newLocationIds: string[] (the FULL updated set, not a delta), newServiceTier?: string, newTotalValueCents, newAgreementValueCents}. Meant to be called by a rep action (Deals Desk, not built) or a future upsell-acceptance webhook once one exists - nothing in this repo yet generates this call automatically.

nodes.name: Fetch old Contract
nodes.notes: Captures the BEFORE state (tier, totalValue, locationIds) for the AccountingAuditEvent below - the whole point of an audit event is a real before/after, not just an after.

nodes.name: Create new Contract

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ companyId: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.companyId, locationIds: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.newLocationIds, status: 'Active', totalValue: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.newTotalValueCents, agreementValue: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.newAgreementValueCents, tier: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.newServiceTier || ($json.data || $json).tier, startedAt: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: A NEW Contract row, not a PATCH to the old one - 'triggers versioning, NOT an edit in place' is the spec's own explicit wording. Falls back to the old Contract's own tier when the caller didn't name a new one (a pure Location-count change with no tier change).

nodes.name: Supersede old Contract
nodes.notes: 'Old Contract -> status changes to Superseded (never deleted - audit trail requires the history)' - per spec, verbatim. supersededByContractId is the field CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's Contract object already reserved for exactly this, unused until now.

nodes.name: Create AccountingAuditEvent

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ companyId: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.companyId, oldContractId: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.oldContractId, newContractId: $('Create new Contract').item.json.id, beforeTotalValueCents: ($('Fetch old Contract').item.json.data || $('Fetch old Contract').item.json).totalValue, afterTotalValueCents: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.newTotalValueCents, beforeLocationIds: ($('Fetch old Contract').item.json.data || $('Fetch old Contract').item.json).locationIds, afterLocationIds: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.newLocationIds, occurredAt: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: New object this pass, CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's AccountingAuditEvent - 'auto-logs: old Contract ID -> new Contract ID, what changed, before/after values, timestamp,' per spec verbatim. Distinct from the generic Activity Event timeline (which logs Tag-for-Action and AI Activity Summary entries) - this is specifically the financial/contract change record #accounting (Section 14's new channel) surfaces.

nodes.name: Advance Opportunity to Expansion
nodes.notes: 'Deal stage on the affected record moves to Expansion - distinct from new-logo pipeline stages (Demo Queue etc. don't apply to an existing client expanding)' - per spec verbatim. This is why opportunityId is a required input: Expansion is a stage on a real Opportunity representing the upsell deal, not an automatic side effect with no deal record to advance.

nodes.name: Split newLocationIds
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget branch relative to the response - same reasoning as stripe-payment-to-crm.workflow.json's own Location-status-update branch. Reads directly off the webhook's own output (this branch never needed an intermediate node's $json), same as that workflow's pattern.

nodes.name: Update Location contractStatus
nodes.notes: Covers a newly-ADDED Location on the amended Contract (one that wasn't on the old Contract's set) - needs its contractStatus/companyId set for the first time, same as W1.6's own Won-conversion write. A Location that was already on the old Contract and stays on the new one gets the same PATCH again here, which is a harmless no-op re-write, not a bug - simpler than diffing old vs. new sets to skip unchanged ones. Same ActiveM2M-assumed simplification flagged in W1.6.

nodes.name: Fetch old Contract's Billing Periods
nodes.notes: 05 Section 15: 'Contract Amendments close out the current period and start a new one at the updated value - no need to rewrite historical periods.' There's no explicit 'is this the open one' flag on BillingPeriod (CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's fields: periodStart/periodEnd/revenueCents/cogsBreakdown/commissionOwedCents/commissionStatus/repId, none named 'closed') - the next Code node picks the most-recently-started period as 'current' rather than trusting a status field that doesn't exist.

nodes.name: Pick current period
nodes.notes: KNOWN LIMITATION, flagged rather than silently assumed correct: picking the latest-started period as 'current' is a heuristic, not a guarantee - if periods are ever created out of order, or a Contract somehow has zero periods (shouldn't happen once W1.6 always creates period #1, but not enforced), this could pick the wrong one or find none. currentPeriodId: null is handled explicitly downstream (the close-period PATCH is skipped, not sent with a broken URL).

nodes.name: Close current period
nodes.notes: Truncates the old Contract's open period early (periodEnd = now, whatever it was previously) rather than deleting it - the period still holds whatever revenue/COGS/commission accrued on the old terms up to this moment, which is exactly the historical record Section 15 says not to rewrite.

nodes.name: Create new period

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contractId: $('Create new Contract').item.json.id, periodStart: new Date().toISOString(), periodEnd: new Date(Date.now() + 30*24*60*60*1000).toISOString(), revenueCents: 0, commissionStatus: 'accrued' }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Start a new one at the updated value' - revenueCents starts at 0 rather than the new agreementValue, since revenue is Stripe-linked (an actual payment event), and an Amendment doesn't necessarily involve an immediate new Stripe charge (could be a mid-cycle upsell billed on the next cycle). Runs unconditionally, not gated behind 'Has a current period?', since a new Contract needs its first period regardless of whether the old one was found/closeable - matches W1.6's own 'always create period #1' rule.

nodes.name: Alert: Contract Amendment logged

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'info', source: 'contract-amendment-flow', message: 'Contract Amendment logged for Company ' + $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.companyId + ' - Contract ' + $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.oldContractId + ' superseded by ' + $('Create new Contract').item.json.id + '.', linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/company/' + $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.companyId }) }}

nodes.notes: 'Contract Amendment logged (new)' is explicitly named in 05 Section 11's alert-trigger list, and Section 14 names #accounting as the channel it belongs in - not an invented alert.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, newContractId: $('Create new Contract').item.json.id, oldContractId: $('Contract amendment webhook').item.json.body.oldContractId }) }}
